issue.title: Race in bytes_hash under free-threading

labels.name: type-bug
labels.description: An unexpected behavior, bug, or error

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

Run the following reproducer under Python 3.13.1t with free-threading enabled:
```python
import concurrent.futures
import functools
import threading

num_threads = 8

def closure(b, x):
  b.wait()
  x.__hash__()

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_threads) as executor:
  for _ in range(100):
    b = threading.Barrier(num_threads)
    x = b"hi"
    x = x * 100000
    for _ in range(num_threads):
      executor.submit(functools.partial(closure, b, x))
```

PyBytesObject::ob_shash probably needs to be read and written atomically.

### CPython versions tested on:

3.13

### Operating systems tested on:

Linux

* gh-130022

comments.body: I think this is just a matter of using relaxed atomics in `bytes_hash` to access `ob_shash` and checking if any of the other uses of `ob_shash` need atomic operations.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/043ba8ac-796c-4e07-b203-91ffedaf4a79)
Hi, I would like to work on this issue, but I have not been able to replicate it as shown in the image. I built CPython from the 3.13 branch using the following command to enable free-threading `./configure --without-threads`

Please let me know how I can replicate this issue. Thanks!

The flag for building with free threading enabled is `--disable-gil`. If you also want a debug build with thread sanitizer, you should use:

```
./configure --with-pydebug --disable-gil --with-thread-sanitizer
```

Hi,

Thanks for the comment. However, I am running into the following issue using your command:

`./configure --with-pydebug --disable-gil --with-thread-sanitizer`

which gives the following error:
`checking for --with-mimalloc... configure: error: --disable-gil requires mimalloc memory allocator (--with-mimalloc).`

and then using:
` ./configure --with-pydebug --with-mimalloc --disable-gil --with-thread-sanitizer`

gives:
` --with-mimalloc... configure: error: mimalloc requires stdatomic.h, use --without-mimalloc to disable mimalloc.`
You'll need a compiler that has support for stdatomic.h. I think GCC 5.1 (9+ years old) or newer should work as will any comparably recent version of clang.

Yup already using that

```
# gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 14.0.1 20240411 (Red Hat 14.0.1-0)
Copyright (C) 2024 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
```

I'm not sure what the issues is then. Make sure you have the dependencies installed and follow the steps at https://devguide.python.org/getting-started/setup-building/#build-dependencies.

Also, it's worth making sure that the compiler used by `configure` is the same as the run you are running manually. That's not always the case!
Thanks for your help! I will take a look.

In case if this can help, we wrote also a section here on compiling free-threaded CPython with TSAN + foundational packages like NumPy: https://py-free-threading.github.io/debugging/#compiling-cpython-and-foundational-packages-with-thread-sanitizer-tsan

Thanks for the helpful comment, I just found the error originates from `--with-thread-sanitizer` flag. The following error is shown in the config.log. 
```
configure:17425: checking for stdatomic.h
configure:17448: gcc -pthread -o conftest   -fsanitize=thread  conftest.c  >&5
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find libtsan_preinit.o: No such file or directory
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
configure:17448: $? = 1
configure: failed program was:
| /* confdefs.h */
```

Removing this flag allows for the config to built without any errors but the make fails to import on `_sha2` with the error.

```
Following modules built successfully but were removed because they could not be imported:
_sha2    

[ERROR]  _sha2 failed to import: /workspaces/codespaces-blank/cpython/build/lib.linux-x86_64-3.13-pydebug/_sha2.cpython-313td-x86_64-linux-gnu.so: undefined symbol: __tsan_read_range
```

So, it looks like there is an issue with how TSAN is configured/installed on my system and I will try your guide to see if that elevates the issue!

Thanks for your help! I appreciate it.

I personally use docker containers to build cpython with clang+TSAN+free-threading, here is how you can install everything and build cpython inside a docker container:
```bash
cd cpython
docker run -it \
    -v $PWD:/cpython \
    -w /cpython \
    --name=cpython-dev-nogil-tsan \
    --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN \
    --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
    --network=host --security-opt seccomp:unconfined --ipc=host \
    ubuntu@sha256:b359f1067efa76f37863778f7b6d0e8d911e3ee8efa807ad01fbf5dc1ef9006b \
    /bin/bash

# Inside the docker container:
apt-get update && ln -fs /usr/share/zoneinfo/Europe/Paris /etc/localtime && \
    apt-get install -y tzdata && \
    dpkg-reconfigure --frontend noninteractive tzdata
    apt-get install -y git wget cmake --no-install-recommends && \
    apt install -y ccache clang-18 libstdc++-14-dev build-essential libssl-dev \
            zlib1g-dev libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev curl git \
            libncursesw5-dev xz-utils tk-dev libxml2-dev libxmlsec1-dev \
            libffi-dev liblzma-dev

    cd /cpython && \
    CC=clang-18 CXX=clang++-18 ./configure --disable-gil --with-thread-sanitizer --prefix $PWD/output-python && \
    make -j 8 && \
    make install && \
    export PATH=$PWD/output-python/bin:$PATH && \
    python3.13t -VV && \
    python3.13t -m pip --version && \
    PYTHON_GIL=0 python3.13t -c "import sys; print(sys._is_gil_enabled())"
```
The drawback of the approach maybe if you are not comfortable with gdb for debugging and using terminal to execute any command.

HTH
Thanks for your help! The error is reproducible now. I will get down to debugging and fixing it.
